text:
maria: Heads up — prod inference fleet in us-west-2 is seeing intermittent connection timeouts to the GPU nodepool (llm-inference). Started ~09:12 UTC, upstream resets and 502s from edge.

kai: I see it too. ~20% of requests failing with connection reset. Some pods on gpu-pool-b in CrashLoopBackOff.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: [alert] route 502: upstream connection reset — incident created (#INC-4291).

jordan: Quick cluster snapshot:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-b -o wide
NAME           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-b-node-07  NotReady   <none>   78d  v1.28.2
gpu-b-node-08  Ready      <none>   12d  v1.28.2
gpu-b-node-09  Ready      <none>   3d   v1.28.2
```
kubelet logs for gpu-b-node-07 show repeated `connection reset by peer` to kube-proxy.

kai: Also seeing terraform state lock when trying to adjust nodepool size: 
```
Error: Error acquiring the state lock
Terraform is already locked by... (ID: 0a1b2c3d)
``` 
I can't run a plan until lock cleared.

maria: Flux tried to reconcile the helm release and failed. Policy webhook returned `deny` for a patched DaemonSet due to nodeSelector mismatch (`inference=llm` vs `inference=true`). That caused partial pod churn.

leo: That aligns with the chart change yesterday — helm values switched label to `inference=llm` (PR #642). The overlay in gitops still expects `inference=true`. So during reconcile some pods got scheduled differently.

anya: We should pause reconciliation while we rollback. Suggest: `flux suspend kustomization inference-prod` -> rollback helm release to previous chart (1.4.2) -> wait for pods to stabilise -> unpause.

sre-oncall: Pausing now and performing rollback.

sre-oncall: ```
$ flux suspend kustomization inference-prod
kustomization.infra.fluxcd.io/inference-prod suspended

$ helm rollback gpu-sidecars 3 -n inference-prod
Rollback complete
```

ops-bot: flux: kustomization.infra.fluxcd.io/inference-prod suspended by sre-oncall.

jordan: After pause I tried `terraform plan` to align node labels but still saw the lock. @ops-gcp any idea who held it?

ops-gcp: I found a stale CI run that didn't release the lock. I ran `terraform force-unlock 0a1b2c3d` after coordinating with the CI owner.

kai: Lock released. Re-ran `terraform plan` and applied the label fix to the nodepool mapping.

maria: Rolling pods back and monitoring. So far no 502s in the last 6 minutes and GPU nodes return to Ready. Looks stable.

leo: Postmortem action items:
- Add preflight check in GitOps pipeline to assert helm values vs overlays for nodeSelector labels.
- Add a test in infra CI to detect state-lock retention and surface owner links.
- Add playbook step: pause flux before any emergency helm rollback to avoid conflicting reconciles.

anya: I'll own the GitOps preflight check (OPA policy / kustomize diff in CI). Will open PR with tests.

maria: Great. Also let's create a short runbook entry for terraform lock during incidents — how to find owner, when to force-unlock, and comms steps.

kai: +1. Thanks everyone. Will keep monitoring the fleet for an hour and then close the incident if stable.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-4291 updated: status -> investigating -> mitigated (monitoring).

maria: Closing loop later with postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
